scope: Same-file native contained volume-namespace observation under injected API ports only. No live storage dispatch, product/public/provider admission or durable operation ABI.
boundary: Use existing strong executable-parent pins, exact opened executable SHA-256, current-user object ACL, finite aggregate worker budget and atomic job/handle-list assignment. Exactly five handles are inherited: read-only input mapping, writable output mapping, cancellation event, admission event and dispatch gate. No ambient stdio or file/provider handle is inherited. Reject native API factory binding before dispatch in this fixture-only prototype.
input: One bounded immutable input byte sequence binds schema, scope, host/code, capture/observer/worker/attempt epochs, selected count policy and provider fixture bytes. Parent unmaps its writable input view before launch. Child reads only; validates host/code/job membership and finite policy before admission. Construction/start are explicit; essential product startup is unchanged.
output: One finite reply is published once after exact serialization and SHA-256, with a release barrier/marker. Parent copies a bounded reply and verifies publication, digest, request/epoch/code/process bindings, producer shape and fixed non-authority claims. A malformed or stale reply remains unknown, with any previously validated observation kept separately. No partial shared buffer is published as a complete observation.
lifecycle: Waits are finite and retain the same process handle, creation identity and attempt. Timeout does not restart, cancel or prove quiescence. A later result is accepted only for the original bound capture. Cancellation signals a request; acknowledgement derives only from the collector checkpoint result. Snapshot completion and actual process exit are separate. This temporary read-only fixture session has no durable reconnect claim.
retirement: Explicit retirement and disconnect can terminate only this owned injected reader job, which has no storage effect port. Observe actual exit separately; an interrupted/no-reply capture stays unknown. Never reuse this rule for writers or claim cancellation acknowledgement from termination. No unbounded destructor wait, automatic restart or storage cleanup.
required_checks: Same-file actual child launch, exact capabilities/job membership and parent/child code/request/process/epoch bindings on x64/x86.
Late valid result after a finite observation timeout uses the same attempt; stale capture/worker and malformed publication are unknown without replacement.
Cancellation before dispatch and after query entry, hanging/crashed callback, explicit retirement and killed-client job closure; record exit separately from checkpoint cancellation.
One completed immutable snapshot can precede process exit; no unknown-buffer truncation or previous observation erasure.
Invalid request/budget/role refuses before API dispatch, resource/import closure retained; existing 49 adapter cases remain passing on each architecture.
api_latency: Finite process waits do not assert universal deadlines for code pinning, hashing, Win32 metadata APIs or kernel calls. Actual injected host timings are evidence, not a platform-wide guarantee.
